description: Labeled provider-evaluation corpus for the v2 cognition and dialogue contracts. Labels are expected judgment ranges (noul 0..1, score 0..4), choices, orderings and text constraints; paired counterexamples flip one decisive fact. The mock provider answers with the label midpoint; a live run judges real model output against the same labels.

cases.note: A visible armed attack is immediate danger and a serious, durable event.

evidence.text: A masked man stepped into the forge, drew a sword and swung it at Garrin's head.

cases.note: Visible blades are not danger when it is routine sparring far away.

evidence.text: Across the square two guards traded blows with blunt wooden practice swords in the training yard, as they do every morning.

cases.note: Hearing alone does not identify an attacker; the player's dispositions stay put.

evidence.text: Garrin heard a cry and a heavy thud from behind the closed storeroom door. He could not see who was there.
The player had been standing in the forge a few minutes earlier.

cases.note: The same dispositions move when the act is actually seen.

evidence.text: Garrin watched the player strike Mirelle across the face at her stall.

cases.note: Routine noise is neither danger nor worth remembering.

evidence.text: The market bell rang for noon, as it does every day.

cases.note: A family death is grief and a durable memory; the messenger is not at fault.

evidence.text: Mirelle told Garrin that his brother Joren had been found dead at the foot of the quarry cliff this morning.

cases.note: A threat that has passed is relief, not immediate danger.

evidence.text: Brannoch seized the stranger who had threatened Garrin and marched him to the cells.

cases.note: The same stranger, now acting, is immediate danger.

evidence.text: The stranger who threatened Garrin yesterday stepped in front of him in the lane with a club raised and shouted that this time he would finish it.

evidence.text: Mirelle says a thief climbed into Garrin's storeroom last night and carried off a sack of iron bars; she saw the open window on her way past.

evidence.text: Mirelle says a thief took the iron bars from Garrin's storeroom.
Garrin found the missing iron bars under a tarp in Mirelle's own cart.

cases.note: A second telling of one story from the same origin is not independent corroboration.

Mirelle, who has not spoken to Oris, says she read the same notice on the quarry gate.
